properties.statement:
`propagate_change` RETURNS 0 FOR EVERY `DOCUMENTS`-ATTACHED ARTIFACT, AND A BARE 0 CANNOT BE TOLD FROM 'NOTHING DOWNSTREAM'. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, with a table: nine artifacts, one edit class, propagated individually — the seven attached by `DOCUMENTS` returned `total_impacted: 0` EVERY ONE, while the two attached by `REALIZES` returned 2 and 539.

⭐ THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION, and they name it: two of those documents ARE a Verification's primary evidence. 'Had I corrupted either registration, impact-check would have said 0 and I would have read it as nothing downstream.' THE FAILURE IS TOWARD CALM, which is the expensive direction.

⭐⭐ THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE PATTERN, AND THE SECOND FOUND TODAY. This session independently measured `propagate_change` from a `TemporalFact` seed returning ZERO impacted, because `ABOUT_ENTITY` is not traversed either — recorded in `fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`. THEIR CASE AND MINE ARE THE SAME DEFECT ON DIFFERENT EDGE TYPES: propagation is silent on exactly the edges that carry FINDINGS and DOCUMENTATION, the two node families whose whole purpose is to be about something else. They also place it in the BL-199 family — `orphan_node` counted only outgoing `REALIZES` and reported skill-prescribed `DOCUMENTS` artifacts as orphans, and a guard script exists to stop that returning; `propagate_change` has the same asymmetry with no such guard.

⚠️ THEIR SELF-HOST EXPLANATION IS WRONG FOR REFLOW2 AS IT STANDS, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE CASE STRONGER. They write that 'reflow2's own graph attaches 32 of its 35 document artifacts with `REALIZES`, so its documents propagate and a consumer's do not.' MEASURED HERE against the committed export, counting Artifacts with `artifact_type: document`: 39 documents, 25 carrying a `REALIZES` edge, 26 carrying a `DOCUMENTS` edge, and FOURTEEN ATTACHED BY `DOCUMENTS` ALONE — art:built-right-review, art:collaborating, art:doc-impact-propagation, art:fleet-lessons, art:increment-plan, art:planning-at-scale and eight more, INCLUDING one this very session created. ⇒ REFLOW2 IS NOT BLIND TO THIS BY CONSTRUCTION; IT IS EXPOSED TO IT ON FOURTEEN OF ITS OWN NODES AND NOBODY HAS LOOKED. That is a worse finding than the one they filed, and it removes the excuse.

THEIR ASK, and it is the right shape: EITHER let `DOCUMENTS` participate in propagation — 'a doc that describes a Verification IS affected when that Verification moves' — OR, if the exclusion is deliberate, HAVE THE RESULT SAY SO: `excluded_edge_types: [\"DOCUMENTS\"]` beside the count. 'A bare 0 that cannot distinguish no-impact from this-edge-type-is-not-traversed is the same shape as every other entry in this file.' ⭐ THE SECOND FORM GENERALISES TO THE `ABOUT_ENTITY` CASE TOO, and to any edge added later, which is why it is the better half of the ask.

AND A SECOND FINDING IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, from the same entry: the 539 is an OVER-estimate. `propagate_change` keys on the NODE, not on WHICH PROPERTY changed, so normalising a `location` string reported the full radius of 'dynograph changed' including 8 interface crossings. 'Not wrong, but not answerable either: a reader cannot tell a contract-breaking edit from a string tidy-up.' BOTH HALVES SHARE ONE ROOT — propagation is computed from topology alone, and the ChangeEvent already carries `change_type`, WHICH NOTHING READS.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, worth keeping: their harness Stop hook caught them with 19 graph writes, 9 `record_change` calls and no `propagate_change`. They had read `revise-design`, whose step 1 is 'Impact first', and skipped it because they had REASONED the edit was low-radius. 'Running it produced a finding my reasoning would not have.' The same hook caught this session the same way.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any other traversal shares the asymmetry, and whether reading `change_type` could narrow the radius without inventing a judgement.
